svg.aria-label: A mobile element insertion in Parallax output: the chain explains the inserted SVA_E sequence by jumping to a matching copy on another chromosome and back, which outscores skipping the insert, so the read is reported as three records: the two chr7 flanks, which meet at the insertion site, and the insert placed on its source copy.
svg.text: A mobile element insertion: the insert placed on its source copy
Seeds in an inserted SVA_E match a copy on another chromosome. Jumping there and back costs far less than
the inserted bases earn, so the read is reported as three records: two chr7 flanks and the insert.
adjacent on the read, linked by SA tags
Seeds in the inserted 2 kb hit SVA_E copies across the
genome. The copy on chr10 explains the most read bases,
so the chain uses it; shorter matches elsewhere lose.
Explaining the insert beats skipping it
Explaining wins once about 64 inserted bases match:
Each chromosome change starts a record
Records 1 and 3 hold the chr7 flanks, which meet at the
insertion site. Record 2 places the inserted sequence on
its source copy, naming the element that was inserted.
Weak matches stay in one record
If too little of the insert matches, skipping wins: the
flanks are joined in one chr7 record, with the insert
Schematic, not to scale; chromosomes and coordinates are illustrative. Default parameters; bits = −log2 P.
